metadata.title: Fortran Programming Language Knowledge Graph
metadata.subject: Detailed directed graph of Fortran history and standards, language constructs, data types, modules and procedures, arrays, numerical facilities, I/O, parallel programming, interoperability, compilers, libraries, scientific domains, performance, portability, testing, and modernization.

source_basis.primary: User-provided Fortran article excerpt plus curated technical synthesis of language features, standards, compilers, libraries, and software-engineering practices.
source_basis.source_note: The supplied article supports the historical timeline, naming, John Backus and IBM origins, standards evolution through Fortran 2023, language features, portability, and scientific/HPC uses. Tooling and library relationships are supplemental synthesis.
source_basis.verification_note: This graph is a broad reference, not a substitute for the normative ISO/IEC Fortran standard or compiler manuals. Feature availability and behavior vary by edition, compiler release, platform, options, and optional support.
source_basis.scope: Identity and design; history and standards; source form; declarations and types; program units and procedures; modules and OOP; arrays and allocation; operators and control flow; intrinsics and numerical semantics; file I/O; coarrays, OpenMP, MPI and accelerators; C/Python interoperability; compilers and build pipeline; libraries and scientific applications; performance, portability, testing, security, and modernization.

metadata.relationship_direction: Relationships are directed from source to target; type and description define their meaning.
metadata.identifier_conventions: Entity IDs are unique lowercase snake_case identifiers. Relationship IDs are sequential rel_NNNNN identifiers. Every relationship endpoint must refer to an existing entity ID.

entities.name: Fortran programming language
entities.description: Compiled, statically typed, multi-paradigm language especially associated with numerical, scientific, engineering, and high-performance computing.

entities.name: John W. Backus
entities.description: IBM computer scientist who proposed and led the original Fortran project.

entities.name: IBM
entities.description: Computing company that developed the original Fortran system.

entities.name: IBM 704
entities.description: Early IBM scientific computer targeted by the original Fortran system.

entities.name: Fortran-lang community
entities.description: Community ecosystem supporting Fortran education, tools, packages, and development.

entities.name: International Organization for Standardization (ISO)
entities.description: International standards organization involved in publishing the modern Fortran standard family.

entities.name: International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC)
entities.description: International standards organization collaborating with ISO on Fortran standards.

entities.name: ISO/IEC 1539
entities.description: International standard family specifying the Fortran language.

entities.name: FORTRAN I
entities.description: Initial released Fortran system for the IBM 704.

entities.name: FORTRAN II
entities.description: Early revision adding separately compiled subroutines and functions, CALL/RETURN, and COMMON.

entities.name: FORTRAN IV
entities.description: Pre-standard dialect adding explicit declarations, LOGICAL, Boolean expressions, and logical IF.

entities.name: FORTRAN 66
entities.description: First industry-standard edition of Fortran, based largely on FORTRAN IV.

entities.name: FORTRAN 77
entities.description: Edition adding block IF, CHARACTER, improved file I/O, PARAMETER, and other widely used facilities.

entities.name: Fortran 90
entities.description: Major revision introducing free-form source, modules, array syntax, dynamic allocation, derived types, and structured control flow.

entities.name: Fortran 95
entities.description: Revision adding or refining PURE/ELEMENTAL procedures, WHERE/FORALL features, and allocation semantics.

entities.name: Fortran 2003
entities.description: Major revision adding object-oriented features, C interoperability, procedure pointers, and enhanced I/O.

entities.name: Fortran 2008
entities.description: Edition adding or formalizing coarrays, DO CONCURRENT, submodules, and related features.

entities.name: Fortran 2018
entities.description: Edition incorporating prior technical specifications and expanding parallel and interoperability facilities.

entities.name: Fortran 2023
entities.description: Current standard edition, published in November 2023, with targeted additions and corrections.

entities.name: 1956 Fortran reference manual
entities.description: First Fortran programmer's reference manual for the IBM 704, published in October 1956.

entities.name: Fortran standardization
entities.description: Standards define syntax and semantics to improve compatibility across implementations.

entities.name: Fortran design goals
entities.description: Emphasizes mathematical notation, efficient compiled numerical code, array operations, and scientific productivity.

entities.name: Fortran compilation model
entities.description: Compiler translates source into object code or another executable representation before linking and execution.

entities.name: Fortran source code
entities.description: Text containing declarations, program units, statements, comments, and source-form conventions.

entities.name: Fortran object code
entities.description: Compiler-produced object code and metadata consumed by a linker.

entities.name: Fortran executable
entities.description: Linked executable assembled from object files and required libraries.

entities.name: Fortran runtime library
entities.description: Runtime support for language features such as I/O, allocation, and error handling.

entities.name: Source-to-binary build pipeline
entities.description: Flow from source processing and semantic analysis through optimization, code generation, linking, and loading.

entities.name: Compiler front end
entities.description: Processes source form, parses syntax, resolves names, and performs semantic checks.

entities.name: Compiler optimizer
entities.description: Transforms eligible code while preserving the semantics required by the selected language mode and options.

entities.name: Compiler backend
entities.description: Generates target-specific machine code and object representation.

entities.name: Linker
entities.description: Resolves symbols and combines object files and libraries into executables or libraries.

entities.name: Program loader
entities.description: Operating-system/runtime component that loads and starts an executable.

entities.name: Fixed-form source

entities.name: Free-form source
entities.description: Modern source form with flexible indentation and ampersand continuation.

entities.name: 80-column punched cards
entities.description: Historical medium that influenced fixed-form column conventions.

entities.name: Case-insensitive identifiers
entities.description: Fortran keywords and identifiers are generally case-insensitive.

entities.name: Identifier

entities.description: Source text ignored by the compiler.

entities.name: Line continuation

entities.name: INCLUDE statement

entities.name: Fortran preprocessing

entities.name: INTEGER

entities.name: REAL
entities.description: Finite-precision real floating-point type.

entities.name: DOUBLE PRECISION
entities.description: Named higher-precision real type from earlier language conventions.

entities.name: COMPLEX
entities.description: Type representing real and imaginary components.

entities.name: LOGICAL

entities.name: CHARACTER

entities.name: Derived type

entities.name: Kind parameter

entities.description: Legacy rule inferring types from identifier initial letters unless overridden.

entities.description: Requires explicit declarations and prevents accidental reliance on implicit typing.

entities.name: PARAMETER

entities.name: INTENT

entities.name: OPTIONAL
entities.description: Allows a dummy argument to be omitted when the interface supports it.

entities.name: ALLOCATABLE
entities.description: Declares an object whose storage can be dynamically allocated and released.

entities.name: POINTER
entities.description: Declares pointer association semantics.

entities.name: TARGET
entities.description: Allows an object to be a target for pointer association.

entities.name: DIMENSION
entities.description: Specifies array rank and bounds.

entities.name: SAVE
entities.description: Requests persistence of local state across procedure invocations.

entities.name: VOLATILE
entities.description: Constrains assumptions about changes by mechanisms outside ordinary visible assignment.

entities.name: CONTIGUOUS
entities.description: Specifies contiguity requirements for eligible pointer or assumed-shape entities.

entities.name: BIND(C)
entities.description: Declares supported interoperability with C conventions.

entities.name: VALUE
entities.description: Provides value-passing semantics for eligible interoperable dummy arguments.

entities.name: PROTECTED
entities.description: Restricts definition of a module entity outside its defining module/submodules.

entities.name: SELECTED_REAL_KIND
entities.description: Selects a real kind by precision/range requirements.

entities.name: SELECTED_INT_KIND
entities.description: Selects an integer kind by range requirements.

entities.name: ISO_FORTRAN_ENV
entities.description: Exposes environment constants, I/O units, and named kinds where available.

entities.name: Program unit
entities.description: A main program, module, submodule, subroutine, function, or other supported unit.

entities.name: Main program
entities.description: Top-level program unit defining the program entry point.

entities.name: MODULE
entities.description: Encapsulates declarations, types, data, generic interfaces, and procedures.

entities.name: SUBMODULE
entities.description: Separate implementation unit associated with a parent module.

entities.name: SUBROUTINE
entities.description: Procedure invoked for effects and optional output arguments.

entities.name: FUNCTION
entities.description: Procedure that returns a result usable in expressions where permitted.

entities.name: Internal procedure
entities.description: Procedure contained within another program unit and able to use host association.

entities.name: External procedure
entities.description: Procedure defined outside the current scoping unit.

entities.name: Module procedure

entities.name: Generic interface
entities.description: Maps a generic name to specific procedures based on argument characteristics.

entities.name: Explicit interface

entities.name: ABSTRACT INTERFACE
entities.description: Specifies procedure characteristics without implementation.

entities.description: Pointer associated with a compatible procedure.

entities.name: RECURSIVE procedure
entities.description: Procedure explicitly permitted to call itself directly or indirectly.

entities.name: PURE procedure
entities.description: Procedure restricted from certain side effects.

entities.name: ELEMENTAL procedure
entities.description: Scalar procedure semantics applied element-wise to arrays.

entities.name: Type-bound procedure
entities.description: Procedure bound to a derived type and invoked through an object or type.

entities.name: Final procedure
entities.description: Procedure used for eligible object finalization.

entities.name: Type extension
entities.description: Extends an extensible derived type with additional components and behavior.

entities.name: Polymorphism
entities.description: Allows use of objects through parent/class interfaces with dynamic type behavior.

entities.name: SELECT TYPE
entities.description: Selects a branch based on dynamic type.

entities.name: SELECT RANK
entities.description: Selects a branch based on the rank of an assumed-rank entity.

entities.name: USE statement

entities.name: ONLY clause

entities.name: Use association

entities.name: Keyword arguments

entities.name: Array
entities.description: Indexed collection of elements with rank, shape, and bounds.

entities.name: Array rank

entities.name: Array shape
entities.description: Extent in each dimension.

entities.name: Array bounds
entities.description: Lower and upper index bounds.

entities.name: Array section

entities.name: Array constructor

entities.name: Array expression
